analysis:
Integration of all 29 units. The PR is mostly documentation (changelog.d, docs/architecture/inference.md 3541-3575, docs/developer/test.md, docs/provider/two-mac-cluster.md) plus a small cluster-service change. ClusterSetupLinkExchange.swift adds Pairing.Identity (public pins, clusterID, linkEpoch, edgeID; the edge secret is excluded) and Responder.pairing, which records the key the listener answers with. ClusterService.swift replaces cableMove with listenerChange, which adds .pairingChanged and .unpaired. It adds an internal injectable Listening (ports, policy, selection) whose production default keeps the fixed ports and .thunderboltOnly. ClusterServiceControl.swift makes ensureControlResponder follow the pairing, and ensureControl now also drops the control node when node.localID differs from pairing.localMemberID. Tests are registered and added (loopback only, test-only .loopbackForTests policy).

Security effect is net positive. Before, a listener kept the old pairing's edge secret after re-pair or unpair and was stuck refusing handshakes. Now it rekeys, or stops when no pairing exists. Rejection of stale pairings stays fail-closed (handshakeRejected). An unreadable pairing store leaves listeners unchanged, which is the same posture as before and which the docs state explicitly. This is a plausible but non-regressive tradeoff. Compared with the prior behavior, it does not widen any access.

Verified from supplied patch text: the Identity excludes the secret, and the production Listening defaults are unchanged. Not directly seen: the full head bodies of listenerChange, ensureResponder and Listening in ClusterService.swift (only the patch excerpt and the base text were available). Residual unverified items: that listenerChange cannot be triggered by an unauthenticated peer, that the old responder is always stopped before a new one is bound, and that the restart log line does not leak secrets (the docs show only the cluster label). The cluster pairing boundary has no entry in the canonical threat model (closest: TB-003 and TB-002), which may be a threat-model gap but not a regression. No findings. A deeper pass over the ClusterService.swift head hunks is advisable.
